AI.tldr: SAMRI-3D presents the largest MRI-only segmentation benchmark (10,392 volumes, 34 datasets) and a method fine-tuning SAM2's lightweight decoder/memory modules with frozen image encoder, achieving 0.76 mean Dice. It further introduces Global Volume Tokens (GVT) with a TSDF reconstruction objective (discarded at inference) that raises performance to 0.78 Dice with zero added cost and strong generalization to unseen datasets.
AI.motivation: Existing SAM adaptations to medical imaging are general-purpose and treat MRI as one modality among many; large-scale MRI-specific modeling and benchmarking are limited despite MRI's inherently low soft-tissue contrast making many boundaries invisible on individual slices.
AI.method: (1) SAMRI-3D benchmark: 10,392 volumes from 34 datasets (27 public, 7 in-house), 12 anatomical domains, 10+ sequences, with seen/unseen splits. (2) Freeze SAM2 image encoder, fine-tune only lightweight decoder and memory modules. (3) Global Volume Tokens (GVT): persistent memory tokens trained with a Truncated Signed Distance Field (TSDF) reconstruction objective, discarded at inference (zero added cost).
AI.result: Fine-tuning raises Dice from 0.58 (zero-shot) to 0.76, surpassing SAMed-2 (0.69), Medical-SAM2 (0.49), SAM-Med3D (0.37). Full SAMRI-3D (with GVT) achieves 0.78 Dice with lowest variance across all 34 datasets, and uniquely shows no drop on 8 held-out datasets (0.79 unseen vs. 0.78 seen).
AI.conclusion: MRI-specific fine-tuning of SAM2 with lightweight modules and TSDF-informed Global Volume Tokens yields state-of-the-art 3D MRI segmentation with strong generalization and zero inference overhead.

title: Totally Positive Matrices and the Highest-Order Coefficients of the Characteristic Polynomial
comment: 26 pages, 12 figures, 3 tables. Published open access in Linear Algebra and its Applications
summary: We investigate the extent to which totally positive matrices can be distinguished through the highest-order coefficients of their characteristic polynomials. To identify the most informative coefficients, we also employed neural-network classifiers together with feature-attribution methods. Using datasets built from several structured totally positive families, including products of positive bidiagonal matrices, Vandermonde matrices, and Cauchy matrices, we find that the coefficients (a_{n-1}, a_{n-2}, a_{n-3}) already contain strong discriminatory information for separating totally positive from non-totally positive matrices in dimensions 5, 10, and 30. The resulting separation is markedly nonlinear and admits a natural geometric description in the corresponding three-dimensional coefficient space by means of Mahalanobis ellipsoids. These ellipsoids enclose the totally positive samples while excluding most non-totally positive ones. Moreover, different structured totally positive families exhibit distinct ellipsoidal signatures, and the separation between these signatures increases with the dimension. These observations lead us to formulate a conjecture on the geometric separation of structured totally positive families in the space determined by the three highest-order characteristic coefficients.

AI.tldr: Totally positive matrices can be distinguished from non-totally positive ones using the three highest-order characteristic polynomial coefficients (a_{n-1}, a_{n-2}, a_{n-3}), with neural networks confirming their discriminatory power. Separation forms Mahalanobis ellipsoids in coefficient space, and different structured families show distinct, dimension-increasing ellipsoidal signatures, leading to a geometric separation conjecture.
AI.motivation: To determine whether totally positive matrices can be distinguished via highest-order characteristic polynomial coefficients, and to identify the most informative coefficients for classification using neural-network feature attribution.
AI.method: Built datasets from structured totally positive families (products of positive bidiagonal, Vandermonde, Cauchy matrices), used neural-network classifiers with feature-attribution methods to identify informative coefficients, and analyzed geometric separation via Mahalanobis ellipsoids in the three-dimensional space of highest-order coefficients.
AI.result: Coefficients (a_{n-1}, a_{n-2}, a_{n-3}) provide strong discriminatory information for separating totally positive from non-totally positive matrices in dimensions 5, 10, and 30. Separation is nonlinear and described by Mahalanobis ellipsoids. Different structured families exhibit distinct ellipsoidal signatures that grow more separated with increasing dimension.
AI.conclusion: The findings suggest a conjecture on the geometric separation of structured totally positive families in the space of the three highest-order characteristic coefficients.

title: Benchmarking NACTI Species Recognition in Long-Tailed Regimes
summary: As with most ``in the wild'' collections of the natural world, the North America Camera Trap Images (NACTI) dataset exhibits long-tailed class imbalance, with the largest class covering over 50% of its 3.7M images. Building on the PyTorch Wildlife model, we systematically evaluate Long-Tail Recognition (LTR) methodologies to benchmark species recognition performance, including specialised loss functions and LTR-sensitive regularisation. Our optimised configuration achieves state-of-the-art 99.40% Top-1 accuracy on the NACTI test split, significantly outperforming standard baselines and previously reported top performances. To assess robustness under domain shifts (e.g., night-time captures, occlusion, motion-blur), we extend our evaluation across three independent reduced-bias test sets (including ENA-Detection, Caltech Camera Traps and Missouri Camera Traps). Across these out-of-distribution (OOD) evaluations, our LTR-enhanced model consistently demonstrates substantially stronger generalisation capabilities compared to standard cross-entropy approaches. However, qualitative and quantitative analyses underline that current LTR optimisations cannot fully overcome representational bottlenecks, resulting in catastrophic predictive breakdown for rare `Tail' classes under severe domain shift. For maximum reproducibility, all dataset splits, key code, and network weights are published with this paper at https://github.com/ZehuaLiuY/Species-Classification.

AI.tldr: This paper evaluates Long-Tail Recognition (LTR) methods on the NACTI dataset (3.7M images, severe class imbalance), achieving 99.40% Top-1 accuracy. LTR-enhanced models show better OOD generalization but still suffer from catastrophic breakdown on rare tail classes under domain shifts.
AI.motivation: The NACTI dataset exhibits extreme long-tailed class imbalance (largest class >50% of 3.7M images), which standard training approaches handle poorly. The paper aims to systematically benchmark LTR methodologies to improve species recognition and assess robustness under domain shifts.
AI.method: Building on PyTorch Wildlife, the authors systematically evaluate LTR methods including specialized loss functions and LTR-sensitive regularization. They evaluate on NACTI test split and three OOD datasets (ENA-Detection, Caltech Camera Traps, Missouri Camera Traps) for robustness under night-time, occlusion, and motion-blur domain shifts.
AI.result: Achieves state-of-the-art 99.40% Top-1 accuracy on NACTI test split. LTR-enhanced model shows substantially stronger OOD generalization than cross-entropy baselines. However, catastrophic predictive breakdown occurs for rare tail classes under severe domain shift, indicating LTR cannot fully overcome representational bottlenecks.
AI.conclusion: Current LTR optimizations improve performance on imbalanced wildlife datasets and generalize better OOD, but cannot fully resolve representational bottlenecks — rare tail classes remain vulnerable to catastrophic failure under domain shifts. All splits, code, and weights are open-sourced.

title: Differentiable Logic Gate Networks for Low-Latency EEG Classification on Edge Devices
comment: Published in the Proceedings of the 39th Canadian Conference on Artificial Intelligence, PMLR 318, pages 377-391, 2026. Conference version: https://proceedings.mlr.press/v318/dharia26a.html
summary: Real-time EEG classification on edge devices is bottlenecked by the floating-point arithmetic of conventional neural networks. We investigated Differentiable Logic Gate Networks (Diff-Logic) as a hardware-native alternative that compiles models into pure Boolean circuits executable via bitwise CPU operations. Through rigorous iso-parameter experiments across four EEG datasets spanning two classification tasks, binary dementia detection and 3-class emotion recognition, we compared Diff-Logic against matched-capacity Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP) and Binarized Neural Network (BNN) baselines at four complexity tiers (50k-500k parameters). On dementia screening, Diff-Logic achieved 80.2% Macro F1, outperforming the MLP baseline by 6.8%. On emotion recognition, the MLP retained a moderate performance advantage but incurred a 2.3$\times$ higher latency and 14$\times$ larger model size when deployed on a power-constrained (7W) Nvidia Jetson Orin Nano CPU (Single-core). Critically, Diff-Logic inference time remained nearly constant across a 10$\times$ increase in model scale, achieving a peak speedup of 2.9$\times$ over MLPs at the largest complexity tier. Our results establish logic-based neural architectures as a practical paradigm for resource-constrained brain-computer interfaces, achieving competitive or superior performance while natively satisfying the latency and memory constraints of portable edge deployment. Code is available on GitHub: https://github.com/Shyamal-Dharia/eeg-difflogic

AI.tldr: This paper explores Differentiable Logic Gate Networks (Diff-Logic) as a hardware-efficient alternative to conventional neural networks for real-time EEG classification on edge devices. By compiling models into pure Boolean circuits executable via bitwise CPU operations, Diff-Logic achieves competitive or superior accuracy compared to MLPs and BNNs while delivering up to 2.9× speedup, near-constant inference time across model scales, and dramatically smaller memory footprints on power-constrained platforms like the Jetson Orin Nano.
AI.motivation: Real-time EEG classification on edge devices is bottlenecked by the floating-point arithmetic of conventional neural networks, motivating exploration of hardware-native Boolean circuit alternatives for resource-constrained brain-computer interfaces.
AI.method: The authors investigate Differentiable Logic Gate Networks (Diff-Logic), which compile models into pure Boolean circuits executable via bitwise CPU operations. They conduct iso-parameter experiments across four EEG datasets spanning binary dementia detection and 3-class emotion recognition, comparing Diff-Logic against matched-capacity MLP and BNN baselines at four complexity tiers (50k-500k parameters).
AI.result: Diff-Logic achieved 80.2% Macro F1 on dementia screening, outperforming the MLP baseline by 6.8%. On emotion recognition, the MLP had a moderate advantage but incurred 2.3× higher latency and 14× larger model size on a power-constrained Jetson Orin Nano CPU. Diff-Logic inference time remained nearly constant across a 10× increase in model scale, achieving a peak speedup of 2.9× over MLPs at the largest complexity tier.
AI.conclusion: Logic-based neural architectures establish a practical paradigm for resource-constrained brain-computer interfaces, achieving competitive or superior performance while natively satisfying the latency and memory constraints of portable edge deployment.

title: When 2D Cues Fail: Improving Image Manipulation Localization with Reliable 3D Geometry
summary: Existing image manipulation localization (IML) methods rely heavily on 2D forensic cues, such as low-level artifacts, noise traces, and semantic inconsistencies in the manipulated image. While effective in many cases, these cues become much less discriminative when manipulated regions are well blended with their surrounding context in appearance. In such cases, a manipulated region may remain locally appearance-consistent, but still violate the geometric structure of the surrounding scene. This limitation motivates us to go beyond purely 2D evidence and introduce geometric reasoning into IML. To this end, we leverage monocular reconstruction to obtain auxiliary geometric cues, including depth and surface normals. However, a key challenge lies in the fact that reconstructed geometry on manipulated images is inherently noisy and cannot be used naively. Rather than treating depth and normals as direct evidence, we estimate their reliability and exploit them selectively for localization. Based on this principle, we design a geometry-aware framework (GFrame) that fuses reliable geometric cues with RGB features and propagates them across scales to improve fine-grained localization. Extensive experiments show that the proposed method achieves excellent performance under limited budget constraints. These results indicate that reliable 3D geometry provides complementary forensic evidence beyond traditional 2D cues for IML. Related code will be released.

AI.tldr: The paper proposes GFrame, a geometry-aware image manipulation localization framework that leverages monocular reconstruction to obtain depth and surface normal cues, estimates their reliability to avoid noisy geometric signals, and fuses them with RGB features to improve localization of well-blended manipulations where traditional 2D forensic cues fail.
AI.motivation: Existing IML methods rely on 2D forensic cues (low-level artifacts, noise traces, semantic inconsistencies) which become ineffective when manipulated regions are well-blended with their surrounding context. The authors identify that geometric structure violations in the 3D scene remain underexploited for localization.
AI.method: Proposes GFrame: leverages monocular reconstruction to extract auxiliary geometric cues (depth and surface normals); estimates the reliability of these reconstructed geometric signals to handle inherent noise; selectively fuses reliable geometric cues with RGB features; propagates fused features across scales for fine-grained localization.
AI.result: Achieves excellent performance under limited budget constraints, demonstrating that reliable 3D geometry provides complementary forensic evidence beyond traditional 2D cues for IML.
AI.conclusion: Introducing geometric reasoning via monocular reconstruction into IML is effective; however, reconstructed geometry on manipulated images is noisy and must be used selectively based on reliability estimation rather than naively. Reliable 3D geometric cues offer complementary forensic signals alongside 2D evidence.

title: The Calibration Channel Determines the Bayes-Error Proxy: An Exact Law for Temperature-Induced Distortion
summary: The soft-label Bayes-error estimator beta(z) = E[min(z, 1-z)] of Ishida et al. estimates the irreducible error of a binary task directly from probability-valued labels. Recent work by Ushio et al. showed that this estimator is fragile when the probabilities are not the true posterior: even perfectly calibrated soft labels can yield a substantially inaccurate estimate, and they propose isotonic calibration as a consistent remedy. We complement that line of work by characterizing exactly how the most widely used post-hoc calibration map -- temperature scaling -- distorts the proxy. We prove an exact, model-free identity reducing the temperature-scaled proxy to the classifier's margin distribution, from which we obtain (i) strict monotonicity in the temperature and (ii) a continuous bijection from the temperature axis onto the open interval (0, 1/2), so that a fixed classifier -- with fixed decisions and fixed 0-1 error -- can be made to report any proxy value whatsoever. Under a Gaussian model of the logits we further derive a two-parameter closed form for the entire proxy-versus-temperature curve. Across CIFAR-10, Fashion-MNIST, and SVHN (eight binary tasks), the proxy varies by 56x to 980x at constant test error, the closed form reproduces the empirical curve to within 0.018, and the calibration temperature that minimizes the expected calibration error does not coincide with any stable proxy value. Our results give a precise, predictive account of the distortion whose existence motivates calibration-based remedies, and they reinforce the practical recommendation that a proxy value is meaningful only together with the mechanism that produced its probabilities.

AI.tldr: This paper proves that temperature scaling, a common calibration method, can arbitrarily distort the soft-label Bayes-error proxy (β(z) = E[min(z, 1-z)]), showing it varies by 56x–980x at constant test error. The authors derive a closed-form expression under Gaussian logits and empirically validate it across eight binary tasks from CIFAR-10, Fashion-MNIST, and SVHN.
AI.motivation: Prior work (Ushio et al.) showed that the soft-label Bayes-error estimator is fragile even with well-calibrated probabilities, and proposed isotonic calibration as a remedy. This paper aims to characterize exactly how temperature scaling—the most widely used post-hoc calibration map—distorts this proxy, providing a precise theoretical account of the distortion.
AI.method: The authors prove an exact, model-free identity reducing the temperature-scaled proxy to the classifier's margin distribution, establishing strict monotonicity in temperature and a continuous bijection from temperature to (0, 1/2). Under a Gaussian model of logits, they derive a closed-form two-parameter expression for the proxy-versus-temperature curve. Empirical validation is conducted on eight binary tasks from CIFAR-10, Fashion-MNIST, and SVHN.
AI.result: A fixed classifier with fixed decisions and fixed 0-1 error can report any proxy value in (0, 1/2). Across eight binary tasks, the proxy varies by 56x to 980x at constant test error. The closed-form reproduces empirical curves within 0.018 error. The calibration temperature minimizing expected calibration error does not correspond to any stable proxy value.
AI.conclusion: Temperature scaling systematically distorts the soft-label Bayes-error proxy in a predictable way. The findings reinforce that a proxy value is only meaningful alongside knowledge of the mechanism that produced its probabilities.

title: Anticipate Before Acting: Future-State-Conditioned Vision-Language Navigation
summary:
End-to-end vision-language navigation (VLN) with causal vision-language models can map instructions and egocentric observations directly to actions, but standard behavior cloning supervises only the next action and does not explicitly train the policy state to be predictive of future visual outcomes. We first ask a diagnostic question: if the policy is given an expert-trajectory future image as privileged input at training and testing time, is that additional visual evidence useful for choosing the current action? (These expert-trajectory future images are unavailable at test time in real deployment, so we use this setting only as a privileged-input diagnostic.) The answer is yes; this sanity check shows that future observations can provide rich, actionable cues.
  We then ask a deployable question: without accessing future images at inference, can we still benefit from future information by using a compressed future visual latent only as training supervision? We propose Future-State-Conditioned VLN (FSC-VLN), which adds a future-query token and aligns its hidden state to a frozen visual embedding $Δ$ steps ahead via a training-only target branch that is removed after training. On R2R val-unseen, FSC-VLN improves SR/OSR/SPL over a StreamVLN-style baseline under two training-data regimes, with larger gains on long-horizon episodes; ablations further support the dual-query design (separating future and action queries).

AI.tldr: FSC-VLN improves vision-language navigation by using future visual information as training-only supervision via a future-query token aligned with a frozen visual embedding, enhancing performance on R2R val-unseen especially for long-horizon episodes.
AI.motivation: Standard behavior cloning for VLN only supervises the next action without training the policy state to be predictive of future visual outcomes. The authors first verify that privileged access to future images improves action selection, then explore whether future information can benefit deployment without test-time access.
AI.method: FSC-VLN adds a future-query token and aligns its hidden state to a frozen visual embedding Δ steps ahead via a training-only target branch that is removed after inference. The dual-query design separates future and action queries.
AI.result: On R2R val-unseen, FSC-VLN improves SR, OSR, and SPL over a StreamVLN-style baseline under two training-data regimes, with larger gains on long-horizon episodes.
AI.conclusion: Future observations provide rich, actionable cues for VLN, and compressed future visual latents can effectively serve as training-only supervision to boost performance without requiring future images at test time.

title: OR Else: A Differentiable Trust Region for Policy Optimization
summary: PPO and the GRPO baseline studied here use clipped surrogate objectives whose favorable-direction saturation introduces an abrupt change in the scalar objective's derivative. We ask whether Output Reset (OR), a smooth one-sided saturation rule, offers a useful alternative for large language model post-training. PPO-OR and GRPO-OR replace the clipped policy term with an OR squared-margin loss in rollout-relative token log-ratio space; the advantage sign determines the update direction, and a token contributes zero direct OR residual after crossing the favorable margin. We compare PPO-clip with PPO-OR under generalized advantage estimation (GAE), and GRPO with GRPO-OR under group-relative advantages, using \texttt{Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct} on Anthropic \texttt{hh-rlhf} with one shared reward model and three seeds per method. Under GAE, PPO-OR has a mean final training-time reward-model score $0.305$ higher than PPO-clip, with a larger observed across-seed spread. Under group-relative advantages, GRPO-OR does not have a higher mean score, but shows a smaller observed spread, a near-zero terminal OR residual, and a declining overshoot fraction, while the matched GRPO clipped-objective trace remains variable. Both group-relative methods exhibit substantially larger rollout-to-current log-ratio displacement than the GAE methods, and OR does not consistently reduce it. Thus, OR changes optimization behavior in both matched comparisons, but the observed reward effect differs between them. At $G=2$, the GRPO-OR diagnostics do not translate into a reward-score gain. Whether larger groups change this outcome remains open. The reported scores are training-time reward-model measurements, not held-out human-preference performance.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates whether Output Reset (OR), a smooth one-sided saturation rule, improves upon clipped surrogate objectives in PPO and GRPO for LLM post-training. PPO-OR shows higher reward scores under GAE, while GRPO-OR shows more stable diagnostics but no reward gain at group size G=2.
AI.motivation: Clipped surrogate objectives in PPO and GRPO have abrupt derivative changes due to favorable-direction saturation. The authors explore whether OR, a smoother alternative, can improve optimization behavior and reward outcomes in LLM post-training.
AI.method: Replace the clipped policy term in PPO and GRPO with an OR squared-margin loss in rollout-relative token log-ratio space. Compare PPO-clip vs PPO-OR under GAE, and GRPO vs GRPO-OR under group-relative advantages, using Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct on Anthropic hh-rlhf with one shared reward model and three seeds per method.
AI.result: Under GAE, PPO-OR achieves a mean final reward score 0.305 higher than PPO-clip but with larger across-seed spread. Under group-relative advantages, GRPO-OR does not have a higher mean score but shows smaller spread, near-zero terminal OR residual, and declining overshoot fraction, while GRPO-clip remains variable. Both group-relative methods show larger log-ratio displacement than GAE methods, and OR does not consistently reduce it.
AI.conclusion: OR changes optimization behavior in both matched comparisons, but the reward effect differs between them. At G=2, GRPO-OR diagnostics do not translate into reward gain. Whether larger groups change this outcome remains open. Reported scores are training-time reward measurements, not held-out human-preference performance.

title: SAR Vessel Detection and Gross Tonnage Estimation from Heterogeneous Datasets for Dark Vessel Identification
summary: Detecting vessels engaging in illegal activities is of paramount importance for maritime security. One of the major goals is to detect dark vessels, ships that disable their transponders to evade surveillance. Deep Learning (DL) models can detect vessels in Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) images, enabling maritime traffic analysis regardless of weather or visibility conditions. However, to detect potential dark vessels, a DL model must select only those that are required to carry a transponder based on their Gross Tonnage (GT). Unfortunately, no public SAR dataset is available for training an end-to-end DL model for vessel detection and GT regression. In this work, we present a framework that leverages heterogeneous image and tabular datasets to solve this task. Our solution combines a multi-task DL framework for predicting the location, vessel type, and physical dimensions of ships, cascaded with a non-parametric model for predicting GT from vessel size and category. We perform GT regression by a KNN that measures sample similarity using a hybrid Euclidean and categorical distance. Experiments show that our solution can predict multiple outputs while remaining competitive with state-of-the-art models on individual subtasks, thus enabling the identification of dark vessels. We publish our code on GitHub https://github.com/PaltrinieriDavide/vesseldetection.

AI.tldr: A framework combining multi-task deep learning (vessel detection, type, and dimension prediction) with a KNN-based non-parametric model for Gross Tonnage regression to identify dark vessels in SAR imagery, using heterogeneous image and tabular datasets.
AI.motivation: Detecting dark vessels (ships disabling transponders) is critical for maritime security. Existing DL models can detect vessels in SAR images but cannot distinguish which vessels are required to carry transponders based on Gross Tonnage. No public SAR dataset exists for end-to-end training of vessel detection with GT regression.
AI.method: A multi-task DL framework predicting location, vessel type, and physical dimensions from SAR images, cascaded with a non-parametric KNN model that predicts GT from vessel size and category using hybrid Euclidean and categorical distance.
AI.result: The solution predicts multiple outputs competitively with state-of-the-art models on individual subtasks, enabling dark vessel identification.
AI.conclusion: The proposed framework successfully enables dark vessel detection by combining heterogeneous data sources and a hybrid modeling approach, with code publicly available on GitHub.

title: A Continual Validation, Updating, and Decision-Making Framework for Self-Adaptive Digital Twins via Robust Model Predictive Control: A Case Study in Additive Manufacturing
summary: Digital Twins rely on surrogate models to mirror physical systems in real time, yet these models can degrade as operating conditions evolve, a phenomenon known as concept drift. Maintaining surrogate fidelity under drift, particularly when models must also capture aleatoric uncertainty, remains an open challenge. Existing adaptive frameworks lack principled mechanisms for detecting when updates are needed, for efficiently adapting models from limited streaming data, and for certifying that updates genuinely improve predictive performance. Here we present an adaptive Digital Twin framework that integrates a Fisher score--based multivariate drift detector, Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) for parameter-efficient continual learning, and a Mann--Whitney $U$ test for online statistical validation. The framework monitors surrogate-model confidence via Fisher score vectors, triggers targeted fine-tuning of fewer than 1% of model parameters upon drift detection, and statistically certifies predictive improvement before deploying the updated surrogate. Applied to a stochastic linear system and a directed energy deposition additive manufacturing process as case studies, the framework successfully detects distributional shifts with short delays and restores both predictive accuracy and uncertainty quantification under abrupt and incremental drift. These results establish a statistically rigorous and computationally tractable pathway for sustaining the trustworthiness of neural-network--based Digital Twins throughout their operational life cycle.

AI.tldr: An adaptive Digital Twin framework is proposed that uses Fisher score-based drift detection, LoRA for efficient model updates, and Mann-Whitney U test for statistical validation, enabling surrogate models to maintain predictive accuracy and uncertainty quantification under concept drift with minimal parameters updated.
AI.motivation: Digital Twins rely on surrogate models that degrade over time due to concept drift, yet existing adaptive frameworks lack principled mechanisms for detecting when updates are needed, efficiently adapting from limited streaming data, and certifying that updates genuinely improve predictive performance.
AI.method: The framework integrates three components: (1) a Fisher score-based multivariate drift detector to monitor model confidence, (2) Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) for parameter-efficient continual learning (<1% of parameters updated), and (3) a Mann-Whitney U test for online statistical validation of predictive improvement before deployment.
AI.result: Applied to a stochastic linear system and a directed energy deposition additive manufacturing process, the framework detects distributional shifts with short delays and restores both predictive accuracy and uncertainty quantification under abrupt and incremental drift.
AI.conclusion: The framework establishes a statistically rigorous and computationally tractable pathway for sustaining trustworthiness of neural-network-based Digital Twins throughout their operational life cycle.

title: QIRF Quantum-Inspired Non-Orthogonal Function-Space Compression for 3D Gaussian Splatting
summary: 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) achieves high-quality real-time rendering by representing a scene with a large collection of anisotropic Gaussian primitives. However, complex scenes often require millions of Gaussians, resulting in substantial storage and rendering costs. Existing compression methods mainly reduce redundancy through primitive-wise pruning, attribute quantization, clustering, or neural coding, while redundancy caused by strongly overlapping and non-orthogonal Gaussian basis functions remains largely unexplored. We present QIRF, a quantum-inspired non-orthogonal function-space compression method for 3D Gaussian Splatting. QIRF models neighboring Gaussian primitives as a local non-orthogonal basis and formulates primitive reduction as a subspace-aware selection problem. Specifically, an analytic Gaussian overlap matrix and a radiance-response density matrix are constructed to characterize functional redundancy and rendering relevance. Generalized eigendecomposition is then used to identify the dominant local subspace and select representative Gaussian primitives. An RRDM-based response model and detail-aware safeguarding further preserve visually important high-frequency structures under aggressive pruning. Experiments on 13 scenes from Mip-NeRF 360, Tanks and Temples, and Deep Blending show that QIRF reduces the Gaussian count and raw PLY storage by 71.7 percent on average, corresponding to approximately 3.54 times compression, while maintaining reconstruction quality comparable to 3DGS and achieving a marginal average PSNR improvement of 0.10 dB. QIRF also improves the average rendering speed over 3DGS by 34.3 percent. These results suggest that non-orthogonal function-space redundancy is an important yet underexplored source of representational redundancy in explicit Gaussian radiance fields.

AI.tldr: QIRF is a quantum-inspired compression method for 3D Gaussian Splatting that reduces non-orthogonal functional redundancy among Gaussian primitives via subspace-aware selection, achieving 71.7% reduction in Gaussian count (3.54x compression) with marginal PSNR improvement (+0.10 dB) and 34.3% faster rendering.
AI.motivation: Existing 3DGS compression methods focus on primitive-wise pruning, quantization, clustering, or neural coding, but overlook redundancy caused by strongly overlapping and non-orthogonal Gaussian basis functions, which remains an underexplored source of representational inefficiency.
AI.method: QIRF models neighboring Gaussian primitives as a local non-orthogonal basis, constructs an analytic Gaussian overlap matrix and a radiance-response density matrix (RRDM) to characterize functional redundancy and rendering relevance, then applies generalized eigendecomposition to identify dominant local subspaces and select representative primitives, with RRDM-based response modeling and detail-aware safeguarding to preserve high-frequency structures.
AI.result: On 13 scenes across Mip-NeRF 360, Tanks and Temples, and Deep Blending, QIRF reduces Gaussian count and raw PLY storage by 71.7% on average (~3.54x compression), achieves marginal average PSNR improvement of 0.10 dB over 3DGS, and improves rendering speed by 34.3%.
AI.conclusion: Non-orthogonal function-space redundancy is an important yet underexplored source of representational redundancy in explicit Gaussian radiance fields, and QIRF effectively exploits this redundancy for compression without sacrificing reconstruction quality.

title: FlashRT: Agent Harness for Guiding Agents to Deploy Real-Time Multimodal Applications
summary: Real-time multimodal applications, including voice agents and interactive video generation, compose heterogeneous models into pipelines whose efficient deployment requires application-specific decisions about placement, streaming, and intra-model parallelism. Existing serving systems and auto-parallelism compilers commit to limited transformations and fixed workload assumptions, so achieving high performance on a new application requires hand-crafting an efficient implementation. We present FlashRT, an agent harness that guides coding agents to lift simple developer-written reference implementations into optimized multi-GPU deployments that flexibly weigh target metrics like latency and throughput. Using a new chain-of-program paradigm, FlashRT directs a generic coding agent through a multi-pass transformation process where an agent transforms the reference into an intermediate representation (IR) to capture data dependencies and persistent-state scopes, validates this IR via a sequential interpreter, and performs static analyses to identify candidate transformations. Then, the agent iteratively implements, verifies, and benchmarks each candidate under a measurement-gated optimization loop to produce effective deployments that span different hardware budgets. Across various applications, including video world models and multimodal LLMs, FlashRT converts reference implementations into highly efficient deployments, delivering up to ~70x latency reduction and 2.8x throughput improvement on NVIDIA B200 GPUs. On AMD MI355X GPUs, FlashRT matches the peak latency reduction while increasing peak throughput improvement to 3.6x, demonstrating that agent-driven optimization can be more scalable on platforms with less mature expert optimization. In fact, for Qwen3-Omni text-to-audio inference, FlashRT reduces response latency by 65% compared to the expert vLLM-Omni implementation on AMD MI355X.

AI.tldr: FlashRT is an agent harness that uses a chain-of-program paradigm to guide coding agents in transforming developer-written reference implementations into optimized multi-GPU deployments for real-time multimodal applications, achieving up to 70x latency reduction and 3.6x throughput improvement across different GPU platforms.
AI.motivation: Real-time multimodal applications (e.g., voice agents, interactive video generation) compose heterogeneous models into pipelines whose deployment requires application-specific decisions about placement, streaming, and intra-model parallelism. Existing serving systems and auto-parallelism compilers commit to limited transformations and fixed workload assumptions, forcing developers to hand-craft efficient implementations for each new application.
AI.method: FlashRT introduces a chain-of-program paradigm that guides a generic coding agent through a multi-pass transformation process: (1) transforms the reference implementation into an intermediate representation (IR) capturing data dependencies and persistent-state scopes, (2) validates the IR via a sequential interpreter, (3) performs static analyses to identify candidate transformations, and (4) iteratively implements, verifies, and benchmarks each candidate under a measurement-gated optimization loop.
AI.result: Up to ~70x latency reduction and 2.8x throughput improvement on NVIDIA B200 GPUs; on AMD MI355X GPUs, matches peak latency reduction while increasing peak throughput improvement to 3.6x; for Qwen3-Omni text-to-audio inference, FlashRT reduces response latency by 65% compared to the expert vLLM-Omni implementation on AMD MI355X.
AI.conclusion: Agent-driven optimization can be more scalable on platforms with less mature expert optimization, demonstrating that FlashRT generalizes across different GPU hardware and multimodal applications including video world models and multimodal LLMs.

title: VGOcc: Learning Visual-Geometric Gaussians for Vision-Centric 3D Driving Occupancy Prediction
summary: Vision-only occupancy prediction requires recovering a semantic 3D occupancy field from calibrated surround-view images, where each view provides observations with ambiguous depth along camera rays. Existing methods have progressed from dense structured representations to sparse Gaussian primitives, improving the efficiency of 3D scene representation. However, Gaussian learning still relies primarily on image domain features, which provide limited explicit geometric information for volumetric reasoning. Our key observation is that effective Gaussian occupancy modeling requires not only sparse primitives, but also richer geometric and semantic learning cues. In this paper, we propose VGOcc, which learns visual and geometric cues from foundation models for Gaussian modeling. VGOcc incorporates these cues into primitive initialization and refinement, yielding a representation termed Visual-Geometric Gaussians tailored to semantic occupancy prediction. Specifically, we propose Visual-Geometric Gaussian Birth to form spatially balanced Gaussian centers from ray depth hypotheses, while visual semantic features initialize primitive attributes. Next, we design Pose-Aware Feature Learning to combine foundation tokens with camera embeddings and calibrated ray information. Features from neighboring views are then aggregated at projected 3D locations for each Gaussian refinement stage. Finally, Gaussian decoder refines birth Gaussians with pose-aware features and renders them into semantic occupancy. Experiments on nuScenes demonstrate that VGOcc achieves state-of-the-art performance in vision-only 3D occupancy prediction. Codes will be available at https://github.com/JHLin42in/VGOcc.

AI.tldr: VGOcc proposes Visual-Geometric Gaussians for vision-only 3D occupancy prediction, which uses foundation models to extract geometric and semantic cues for Gaussian primitive initialization and refinement, achieving SOTA on nuScenes.
AI.motivation: Existing Gaussian-based occupancy prediction methods primarily rely on image domain features with limited explicit geometric information for volumetric reasoning, lacking richer geometric and semantic learning cues.
AI.method: VGOcc introduces (1) Visual-Geometric Gaussian Birth that forms spatially balanced Gaussian centers from ray depth hypotheses and initializes attributes with visual semantic features; (2) Pose-Aware Feature Learning that combines foundation tokens with camera embeddings and calibrated ray information; (3) Gaussian decoder that refines birth Gaussians with pose-aware features and renders them into semantic occupancy.
AI.result: Achieves state-of-the-art performance on the nuScenes dataset for vision-only 3D semantic occupancy prediction.
AI.conclusion: Incorporating visual and geometric cues from foundation models into Gaussian primitive initialization and refinement significantly improves occupancy prediction, demonstrating that effective Gaussian modeling requires both sparse primitives and richer geometric/semantic cues.

title: Three-Body Scattering for Generative Modeling
comment: 31 pages, 5 figures, and 4 tables. Code: https://github.com/sp12138/TBSM
summary: Modern generative models typically rely on an adversarial critic, a prescribed noise-to-data path, or an autoregressive factorization. Instead, we show that a proper distributional energy can induce sample-level motion and provide direct regression supervision for a one-step generator. Three-Body Scattering Modeling (TBSM) for generation turns the energy distance into a constant-size per-projectile interaction: each projectile is attracted toward one real source and repelled from one independently generated source. Conditioned on the projectile and its condition, its expectation equals the $2$-Wasserstein gradient-flow velocity of $\frac12D_E^2(P_θ,Q)$. A batch of $B$ frozen-target events yields $O(B)$ sample-level losses, each using one reference for its condition instead of the minibatch-wide all-pairs field used by methods such as Drifting Models. Tracking this conditional expectation online can reduce field noise. Using scattering in frozen image features, TBSM trains one-step generators on ImageNet-256, achieving FID${}=2.23$ with pixel-space PixelDiT-XL and FID${}=1.63$ with latent-space DiT-XL at NFE${}=1$. We provide a design map relating diffusion-related supervision, Drift-like dynamics, and GAN-like objectives. These results establish tracked scattering as a route to high-dimensional one-step generation. Code: https://github.com/sp12138/TBSM.

AI.tldr: TBSM introduces a novel one-step generative modeling framework based on three-body scattering, where each projectile sample is attracted toward a real source and repelled from a generated source, achieving strong FID scores (2.23 pixel-space, 1.63 latent-space) on ImageNet-256 with single-step generation (NFE=1).
AI.motivation: Existing generative models rely on adversarial critics, prescribed noise-to-data paths, or autoregressive factorization. The authors aim to show that a proper distributional energy can directly supervise a one-step generator via sample-level motion without requiring minibatch-wide all-pairs comparisons.
AI.method: TBSM models generation as three-body scattering: each projectile (generated sample) experiences attraction toward one real source and repulsion from one independently generated source, conditioned on the projectile's current state. The conditional expectation of this interaction equals the 2-Wasserstein gradient-flow velocity of half the squared energy distance. A batch of B frozen-target events yields O(B) sample-level losses, using one reference per condition instead of all-pairs fields. Tracking this conditional expectation online reduces field noise.
AI.result: On ImageNet-256, TBSM achieves FID=2.23 with pixel-space PixelDiT-XL and FID=1.63 with latent-space DiT-XL at NFE=1 (single-step generation).
AI.conclusion: TBSM establishes tracked scattering as a viable route to high-dimensional one-step generation, providing a unified design map relating diffusion-related supervision, Drift-like dynamics, and GAN-like objectives.

title: Sparse Evidence Can Suffice: Agentic Evidence Seeking for Multimodal Video Misinformation Detection
summary: Multimodal video misinformation detection is commonly formulated as a holistic video-understanding task, where the entire video and its associated content are processed and judged in a single pass. However, real-world misinformation often exhibits a sparse and compositional evidence structure: a reliable decision may depend on only a few coupled clues, while most video content contributes limited additional information. Exhaustive multimodal reasoning may therefore introduce substantial redundancy and obscure decisive evidence. This motivates decoupling evidence acquisition from verification: first identifying sparse, decision-relevant clues and then judging veracity based on the acquired evidence. Accordingly, we propose SIEVE, a framework for Sparse Interactive Evidence Verification via Extraction in multimodal video misinformation detection. An evidence-seeking agent actively explores the available multimodal evidence and constructs a compact evidence package, which is then used by a verifier to determine veracity. The agent is trained with supervised evidence-seeking trajectories and an evidence-aware reinforcement learning objective that promotes informative evidence acquisition while discouraging unnecessary or invalid interactions. Experiments on multiple video misinformation benchmarks show that SIEVE consistently outperforms the evaluated baselines and supports reliable verification using compact evidence packages. Moreover, the resulting acquisition process provides an explicit and inspectable evidence trail, improving the transparency and groundedness of multimodal misinformation detection.

AI.tldr: SIEVE proposes a decoupled framework for multimodal video misinformation detection that first extracts sparse, decision-relevant evidence via an evidence-seeking agent, then performs verification using compact evidence packages, outperforming baselines while providing inspectable evidence trails.
AI.motivation: Real-world misinformation has a sparse and compositional evidence structure where only a few coupled clues are decisive, while exhaustive holistic reasoning introduces redundancy and obscures key evidence.
AI.method: SIEVE decouples evidence acquisition from verification: an evidence-seeking agent actively explores multimodal evidence to construct a compact evidence package, trained with supervised evidence-seeking trajectories and evidence-aware reinforcement learning, then a verifier judges veracity based on the acquired evidence.
AI.result: SIEVE consistently outperforms evaluated baselines on multiple video misinformation benchmarks, supports reliable verification with compact evidence packages, and provides explicit, inspectable evidence trails.
AI.conclusion: Decoupling evidence acquisition from verification improves both performance and transparency in multimodal video misinformation detection, enabling grounded and inspectable decision-making.

title: Causal Discovery on Irregular Time Series
summary: Causal discovery methods have shown strong performance in temporal systems, but they typically rely on regular and discrete lag structures, limiting their applicability to regularly sampled data. However, many real-world tasks require dealing with irregularly sampled streams of events, such as sensor streams, healthcare data, and financial transactions. In this work, we propose an extension of PCMCI+, a state-of-the-art method for causal discovery on regular multivariate time series, to allow for handling irregular time series. Instead of modelling causal relations through fixed-lag dependencies, our method aggregates causal influence over predefined temporal windows. We evaluate our method on synthetic irregular event streams with known causal structures under different signal-to-noise ratios, showing that it consistently recovers the underlying causal graph and substantially outperforms the standard PCMCI+ on irregularly sampled data.

AI.tldr: This paper extends PCMCI+, a causal discovery method for regular time series, to handle irregularly sampled event streams by aggregating causal influence over temporal windows instead of fixed-lag dependencies, and shows it outperforms standard PCMCI+ on synthetic irregular data.
AI.motivation: Existing causal discovery methods for temporal systems rely on regular and discrete lag structures, limiting their applicability to irregularly sampled data commonly found in real-world applications such as sensor streams, healthcare, and finance.
AI.method: The method extends PCMCI+ by replacing fixed-lag dependency modeling with aggregated causal influence over predefined temporal windows, enabling the handling of irregularly sampled event streams.
AI.result: On synthetic irregular event streams with known causal structures under varying signal-to-noise ratios, the proposed method consistently recovers the underlying causal graph and substantially outperforms standard PCMCI+ on irregularly sampled data.
AI.conclusion: Aggregating causal influence over temporal windows is an effective strategy for extending causal discovery methods designed for regular time series to irregularly sampled event data.

title: SpEmoC: A Balanced Speaker-Segment Multimodal Emotion Benchmark
summary: Understanding human emotions in spoken conversations is a key challenge in affective computing, with applications in empathetic AI, human computer interaction, and mental health monitoring. However, existing datasets vary in scale, emotion distribution, modality alignment, and data partitioning strategies, which can influence reliable cross-dataset generalization and minority-emotion modeling. We introduce SpEmoC a Speaking segment Emotion for Conversations comprising 306,544 raw clips from 3,100 English language movies and TV series. From these, 30,000 high quality, class balanced clips are curated, featuring synchronized visual, audio, and textual modalities annotated for seven emotions through a hybrid pipeline that integrates pretrained models with human validation. SpEmoC uses strict movie- and series-level splits to prevent content overlap between split sets, allowing more reliable evaluation of model generalization. The dataset also maintains a near-balanced distribution across seven emotions, including minority classes such as Fear and Disgust, which supports more balanced learning across categories. Extensive experiments, including in-domain benchmarking, cross-dataset transfer, low-data training, class-imbalance analysis, and modality transfer show that balanced data and careful splitting lead to more stable performance across emotions when models are evaluated on other datasets. These results highlight the importance of dataset design for robust and transferable multimodal emotion recognition.

AI.tldr: SpEmoC is a large-scale multimodal emotion recognition dataset (306K raw clips, 30K curated balanced clips) from movies/TV with strict split strategies, demonstrating that balanced data and careful partitioning improve cross-dataset generalization and minority-emotion modeling.
AI.motivation: Existing emotion datasets vary in scale, emotion distribution, modality alignment, and data partitioning, which hinders reliable cross-dataset generalization and minority-emotion modeling. The authors aim to address these issues by creating a carefully designed dataset with balanced class distribution and strict split strategies.
AI.method: SpEmoC collects 306,544 raw clips from 3,100 English movies/TV series, curates 30,000 high-quality class-balanced clips with synchronized visual, audio, and text modalities, uses a hybrid pipeline combining pretrained models with human validation for annotation, employs strict movie/series-level splits to prevent content leakage, and maintains near-balanced distribution across seven emotions including minority classes.
AI.result: In-domain benchmarking, cross-dataset transfer, low-data training, class-imbalance analysis, and modality transfer experiments show that balanced data and careful splitting lead to more stable performance across emotions when evaluated on other datasets.
AI.conclusion: Dataset design—particularly class balance and rigorous data partitioning—is crucial for robust and transferable multimodal emotion recognition.

title: Occlusion-Aware Panoptic Segmentation with Joint Position Embedding and Occlusion-Level Attention
summary: Panoptic segmentation in complex scenes remains challenging because of occlusions, yet modern approaches often neglect occlusion modelling. In this paper, we propose \textbf{P}osition \textbf{E}mbedding \textbf{M}odulation with \textbf{O}cclusion-\textbf{L}evel \textbf{A}ttention (PEMOLA), a novel occlusion-aware module that can be seamlessly integrated into transformer-based panoptic segmentation. To obtain occlusion cues, we train an occlusion classifier on the COCO-OLAC dataset. The classifier derives the occlusion-level attention, which serves as spatial guidance, while the occlusion labels are encoded into a learnable embedding to produce channel-wise weights. Through joint modulation, PEMOLA elegantly introduces the occlusion priors into the position embedding, thereby improving the occlusion modelling. We further annotate the Cityscapes dataset with occlusion levels, termed Cityscapes Occlusion Labels for All Computer Vision Tasks (Cityscapes-OLAC), following the same labelling protocol as COCO-OLAC, to evaluate the cross-dataset generalisation ability of PEMOLA. Extensive experiments on COCO-OLAC and Cityscapes-OLAC demonstrate that PEMOLA consistently improves panoptic segmentation quality while introducing minimal computational overhead. These results highlight the importance of occlusion modelling, where incorporating occlusion-level attention helps deliver robust panoptic segmentation under occlusion. Code and dataset are available at https://github.com/wenbo-wei/PEMOLA.

AI.tldr: PEMOLA is an occlusion-aware module for transformer-based panoptic segmentation that uses occlusion-level attention and learnable position embeddings to improve performance under occlusions, validated on COCO-OLAC and a newly annotated Cityscapes-OLAC dataset.
AI.motivation: Panoptic segmentation in complex scenes suffers from occlusions, yet modern approaches often neglect occlusion modelling.
AI.method: PEMOLA integrates an occlusion classifier (trained on COCO-OLAC) to derive occlusion-level attention for spatial guidance, and encodes occlusion labels into learnable embeddings for channel-wise weights. These jointly modulate position embeddings to introduce occlusion priors.
AI.result: PEMOLA consistently improves panoptic segmentation quality on both COCO-OLAC and Cityscapes-OLAC with minimal computational overhead.
AI.conclusion: Incorporating occlusion-level attention helps deliver robust panoptic segmentation under occlusion, highlighting the importance of explicit occlusion modelling.

title: O-VAD: Industrial Video Anomaly Detection through Object-Centric Tracking and Reasoning
summary: Industrial Video Anomaly Detection (IVAD) aims to identify anomalous objects and events in an industrial process, which is crucial for modern manufacturing and quality control systems. Existing VLM-based anomaly reasoning methods are capable of detecting open-ended anomalies in general domains. However, their performance declines in industrial settings characterized by intricate object transformations, strict physics, and procedural constraints. To tackle the complexity of such interaction-intensive detection, we introduce a training-free agentic framework for anomaly detection free of domain-specific knowledge, emphasizing object state evolution like humans inspectors. It is designed to track spatial-temporal dynamics and underlying transformations of detected objects over time, and then reason over the object-wise temporal state trajectories to identify abnormal objects in grounded frames. Our method overcomes limitations of prior approaches that rely on retraining on normal clips or injecting domain knowledge as context for test-time inference. Extensive experiments on three IVAD datasets demonstrate that our method outperforms frontier VLMs, agentic frameworks, and traditional VAD methods fine-tuned on the respective datasets, while providing interpretable reports over anomaly processes and types.

AI.tldr: A training-free agentic framework for Industrial Video Anomaly Detection (IVAD) that tracks object state evolution over time, reasons over temporal trajectories to identify anomalies, and outperforms frontier VLMs and traditional VAD methods on three IVAD datasets.
AI.motivation: Existing VLM-based anomaly reasoning methods struggle in industrial settings due to intricate object transformations, strict physics, and procedural constraints. Prior approaches require retraining on normal clips or injecting domain knowledge, limiting their applicability.
AI.method: A training-free agentic framework that tracks spatial-temporal dynamics and object state transformations over time, then reasons over object-wise temporal state trajectories to identify abnormal objects in grounded frames, mimicking human inspectors.
AI.result: Outperforms frontier VLMs, agentic frameworks, and traditional VAD methods fine-tuned on respective datasets across three IVAD datasets, while providing interpretable reports on anomaly processes and types.
AI.conclusion: The proposed training-free approach effectively addresses the complexity of interaction-intensive industrial anomaly detection without requiring domain-specific knowledge or retraining.

title: Plenoptic Condensation: A Novel Approach to Generalized Scene Reconstruction
summary: We present a novel Generalized Scene Reconstruction (GSR) approach called Plenoptic Condensation (PCon). PCon uses a multi-stage reconstruction pipeline, initially converting images into "soupy" scene elements with low (representational) power, then adaptively condensing the "soup" into "structured" elements of higher power capable of efficiently representing, for example, sharp edges and smooth reflective surfaces. PCon scene models called Reality Models (Relms) enable spatially varying representational power, which is essential for high-fidelity rendering, measurement, and scene understanding. We showcase several in-the-wild PCon reconstructions captured with consumer phone cameras and drones. In one case called "Damaged Fiat", PCon is benchmarked against two state-of-the-art (SOTA) GSR methods: NeRO and RT-Splatting. Referring to Figure 1 below, PCon reconstructs the car hood more than twice as accurately as the SOTA methods. But more importantly, the local damage profile error for PCon is 35 um (0.035 mm), whereas the two other SOTA methods are essentially unable to measure the damage at all. Our project website is available at https://quidient.github.io/pcon-2026.html.

AI.tldr: Plenoptic Condensation (PCon) is a multi-stage GSR method that converts images into low-power "soupy" elements and adaptively condenses them into higher-power "structured" elements, enabling spatially varying representational power for high-fidelity scene reconstruction. It significantly outperforms SOTA methods (NeRO, RT-Splatting) on damage profile reconstruction (35 µm accuracy vs. near-zero for baselines).
AI.motivation: Existing GSR methods lack spatially varying representational power, limiting their ability to faithfully reconstruct fine details such as sharp edges, smooth reflective surfaces, and localized damage profiles from in-the-wild captures.
AI.method: A multi-stage reconstruction pipeline: (1) converts images into low-power "soupy" scene elements; (2) adaptively condenses the soup into structured elements of higher representational power. The resulting Reality Models (Relms) enable spatially varying representational power.
AI.result: On the "Damaged Fiat" benchmark, PCon reconstructs the car hood more than twice as accurately as SOTA methods (NeRO, RT-Splatting), with a local damage profile error of 35 µm (0.035 mm) versus the baselines' inability to measure damage.
AI.conclusion: PCon achieves state-of-the-art performance in generalized scene reconstruction, particularly for fine-grained damage measurement, by enabling spatially adaptive representational power through a novel condensation process.

title: Robust Multimodal Dynamic Object Segmentation
comment: Accepted by IEEE International Conference on Robotics & Automation ICRA 2026
summary: Dynamic object segmentation plays a critical role in many visual applications such as static scene reconstruction from dynamic videos. However, existing optical flow-based methods fail to ensure consistent static/dynamic segmentation along object boundaries, while 3D reconstruction-based approaches are highly sensitive to reconstruction errors. To address these limitations, we present a dynamic object segmentation framework that can generate both precise and complete dynamic masks by integrating multimodal cues including 2D point tracks, 3D reconstruction, and semantic information. We design a network combining Transformer architectures with feature clustering aggregation modules to perform static/dynamic classification of multimodal feature trajectories. It enables the model to adaptively determine which type of feature should dominate based on the characteristics of each scene, while also mitigating the impact of feature degradation. Additionally, we introduce a novel point-query-based SAM post-processing method capable of handling multiple objects within a single mask. Extensive experiments demonstrate that our approach achieves state-of-the-art performance in both dynamic object segmentation and static scene reconstruction tasks.

AI.tldr: A dynamic object segmentation framework that integrates 2D point tracks, 3D reconstruction, and semantic cues via a Transformer-clustering network with SAM-based post-processing, achieving SOTA in segmentation and static scene reconstruction.
AI.motivation: Existing optical flow methods produce inconsistent static/dynamic boundaries, and 3D reconstruction-based approaches are overly sensitive to reconstruction errors, limiting performance in applications like static scene reconstruction from dynamic videos.
AI.method: A Transformer-based network with feature clustering aggregation modules for multimodal feature trajectory classification, plus a point-query-based SAM post-processing method that handles multiple objects within a single mask.
AI.result: Achieves state-of-the-art performance in both dynamic object segmentation and static scene reconstruction tasks.
AI.conclusion: Integrating multimodal cues (2D tracks, 3D reconstruction, semantics) with adaptive feature dominance and SAM-based refinement yields precise and complete dynamic masks.

title: Certified Training for Convolutional Perturbations
summary: Vision models have been found to be susceptible to perturbations such as motion blur induced at runtime by a shaking camera. This impedes their deployment in critical applications since phenomena such as slightly blurred vision might lead to failures, for example an object detector missing objects. While methods such as data augmentation or Adversarial Training can improve empirical robustness, they lack formal safety guarantees, making it difficult to identify and mitigate hidden vulnerabilities. We introduce a novel Certified Training approach that leverages an efficient encoding of convolutional perturbations to train provably robust models. Our method significantly outperforms Adversarial Training, achieving, for example, over 80% robust accuracy against motion blur of reasonable intensity on CIFAR10 while maintaining comparable standard accuracy.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces a Certified Training approach that uses efficient encoding of convolutional perturbations to train models that are provably robust against motion blur, achieving over 80% robust accuracy on CIFAR10 while outperforming Adversarial Training.
AI.motivation: Vision models are vulnerable to runtime perturbations like motion blur, which can cause critical failures in deployment (e.g., object detectors missing objects). Existing methods like data augmentation and Adversarial Training improve empirical robustness but lack formal safety guarantees, making hidden vulnerabilities hard to identify and mitigate.
AI.method: The authors propose a Certified Training approach that leverages an efficient encoding of convolutional perturbations to train models with provable robustness guarantees against motion blur.
AI.result: The method significantly outperforms Adversarial Training, achieving over 80% robust accuracy against reasonable-intensity motion blur on CIFAR10 while maintaining comparable standard accuracy.
AI.conclusion: Certified Training with efficient convolutional perturbation encoding provides formal safety guarantees and superior robustness to motion blur compared to empirical methods like Adversarial Training, without sacrificing standard accuracy.

title: HOMIE: Human-object Centric Video Personalization via Multimodal Intelligent Enchancement
summary: Human-object centric video personalization (HOCVP) is a core task within subject-driven video generation. However, existing methods suffer from two key limitations. First, most approaches focusing on inter-subject personalization still struggle to strike a balance between high subject fidelity and accurate interaction patterns between humans and diverse objects, especially when objects represent abstract concepts such as logos. Second, while intra-subject references (e.g., OCR maps, multi-view inputs) are expected to enhance subject fidelity, most existing works lack mechanisms to understand such latent correspondence. To address both challenges, we propose HOMIE, an HOCVP framework that tackles both inter- and intra-subject input settings in a unified manner. Compared to previous approaches, HOMIE proposes a better MLLM integration strategy to extract knowledge of reference-level relationships without compromising the controllability of text encoders or incurring costly re-alignment. Specifically, we introduce global multimodal guidance within self-attention to better align MLLM-derived semantic features with VAE tokens. Furthermore, we propose modality-reference embedding to differentiate tokens from MLLM features and VAE tokens and associate intra-subject reference image tokens. Extensive experiments validate that our method achieves state-of-the-art performance across various HOCVP tasks. Project Page: https://yiyangcai.github.io/homie-page.github.io/

AI.tldr: HOMIE is a unified framework for human-object centric video personalization that handles both inter-subject and intra-subject inputs. It uses MLLM integration with global multimodal guidance in self-attention and modality-reference embedding to achieve high subject fidelity and accurate interaction patterns without costly re-alignment.
AI.motivation: Existing methods struggle to balance high subject fidelity and accurate human-object interaction patterns, especially for abstract objects (e.g., logos). Additionally, most works lack mechanisms to leverage intra-subject references (e.g., OCR maps, multi-view inputs) for enhancing subject fidelity.
AI.method: HOMIE proposes: (1) a better MLLM integration strategy that extracts knowledge of reference-level relationships without compromising text encoder controllability; (2) global multimodal guidance within self-attention to align MLLM-derived semantic features with VAE tokens; (3) modality-reference embedding to differentiate tokens from MLLM features and VAE tokens while associating intra-subject reference image tokens.
AI.result: Extensive experiments validate state-of-the-art performance across various human-object centric video personalization tasks.
AI.conclusion: HOMIE unifies inter- and intra-subject personalization in a single framework, achieving superior subject fidelity and interaction accuracy without costly re-alignment.

title: GigaPath-Flash and GigaTIME-Flash: Efficient Pathology Foundation Models for Whole-Slide and Tumor Microenvironment Analysis
summary:
Foundation models have emerged as a driving force in computational pathology, with the potential to transform cancer diagnosis, prognosis, and treatment selection by learning transferable representations from large-scale histopathology data. A growing landscape of pathology foundation models now spans diverse data sources, architectures, and downstream applications. However, most pretrained models operate only at the image-tile level, use restrictive licenses, and remain computationally expensive, limiting large-scale slide-level clinical and research use.
  Here, we introduce GigaPath-Flash and GigaTIME-Flash, efficient models for whole-slide pathology AI and spatial proteomics prediction. GigaPath-Flash combines a 22M-parameter ViT-S tile encoder with a 21M-parameter LongNet slide encoder, both pretrained on large-scale real-world histopathology data. Its compact tile encoder is distilled from the billion-parameter GigaPath (ViT-g) teacher and shared by both models. GigaPath-Flash retains 97% of GigaPath's average slide-level performance with 50x less compute. GigaTIME-Flash extends this backbone to predict the tumor immune microenvironment directly from routine H&E images. It surpasses the original CNN-based GigaTIME in prediction quality while running 6x faster and using 8x less GPU memory.
  Together with GigaPath and GigaTIME, these models form an open-weight, Apache-2.0-licensed family pretrained on large-scale real-world clinical data. By releasing all models and weights, we provide accessible building blocks for computational pathology, immuno-oncology, and precision health.

AI.tldr: GigaPath-Flash and GigaTIME-Flash are efficient, open-weight pathology foundation models distilled from a billion-parameter teacher. GigaPath-Flash retains 97% of GigaPath's slide-level performance with 50x less compute, while GigaTIME-Flash predicts tumor immune microenvironment from H&E images with 6x speedup and 8x less GPU memory. Both are Apache-2.0 licensed.
AI.motivation: Existing pathology foundation models are limited to image-tile level processing, use restrictive licenses, and are computationally expensive, restricting large-scale slide-level clinical and research applications.
AI.method: GigaPath-Flash uses a 22M-parameter ViT-S tile encoder (distilled from a billion-parameter GigaPath ViT-g teacher) combined with a 21M-parameter LongNet slide encoder, both pretrained on large-scale real-world histopathology data. GigaTIME-Flash extends this backbone to predict tumor immune microenvironment from H&E images.
AI.result: GigaPath-Flash achieves 97% of GigaPath's slide-level performance with 50x less compute. GigaTIME-Flash surpasses the original CNN-based GigaTIME in prediction quality while running 6x faster and using 8x less GPU memory.
AI.conclusion: The models form an open-weight, Apache-2.0-licensed family pretrained on real-world clinical data, providing accessible building blocks for computational pathology, immuno-oncology, and precision health.

title: FlowMimic: Mask-free Visual Editing and Generation with Pixel-pair Warped Flow Field for Online Video Editing Data Generation and Modality Mimicry
comment: Due to file size constraints, the figures in the arXiv file have been heavily lossy-compressed. Please visit the uncompressed file at: https://huggingface.co/datasets/FlowMimic/Uncompressed/blob/main/main.pdf
summary: In line with the prevailing direction of vision research, we explore the integration of both generation and editing capabilities for video and image modalities within a single model. Current approaches to collecting video editing data typically depend on labour-intensive, time-consuming curated procedures--involving object mask annotation, the use of error-introducing pair synthesis via I2V model and ControlNet-like guidance, and VLM-based quality filtering or refinement--and demonstrate limited task scalability. As a result, the diversity of editing tasks remains substantially narrower than that available for image editing models. We develop a pixel-pair temporal warped flow field that can directly generate corresponding video editing samples in real time from image editing samples, and we demonstrate across multiple levels of video editing tasks that a model can learn video editing using only such data. We regard the image modality as a particular form of the video modality. Accordingly, we design a modality mimic generation loss and a modality mimic editing loss to relatively align the capabilities--and thereby the output distributions--of the two modalities through mutual imitation. Moreover, language-based visual editing entails the comprehension of the editing instruction and the reference visual content, the localization of the region corresponding to that instruction within the reference visual contents, and the modification of that region alone. Existing approaches predominantly rely on external aids, such as fine-tuning an additional MLLM or explicitly supplying a mask sequence as auxiliary input during inference. In contrast, we aspire for the model to internalize this capability. To that end, we introduce sense-related tasks--for instance, referring expression segmentation--along with corresponding editing-region-aware latent-level loss and attention-level loss.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes a unified video-image generation/editing model that uses pixel-pair temporal warped flow fields to generate video editing data from image editing data in real time, modality mimic losses to align output distributions, and sense-related tasks with region-aware losses to internalize editing capabilities without external aids.
AI.motivation: Current video editing data collection is labor-intensive, error-prone, and limited in task diversity compared to image editing models. The paper aims to unify video and image editing within a single model without relying on external aids like additional MLLMs or mask sequences.
AI.method: (1) Pixel-pair temporal warped flow field to generate video editing samples from image editing samples in real time. (2) Modality mimic generation and editing losses to align output distributions between image and video modalities. (3) Sense-related tasks (e.g., referring expression segmentation) with editing-region-aware latent-level and attention-level losses to internalize region localization and editing capabilities.
AI.result: Demonstrates across multiple levels of video editing tasks that a model can learn video editing using only image-derived data.
AI.conclusion: Video editing can be effectively learned from image editing data alone using the proposed temporal warping and modality alignment techniques, and models can internalize editing capabilities without external auxiliary inputs.

title: Simple Domain Generalization for Strong Pixel-Level Image Tampering Detection in Modern VLMs
comment: Our code is available at https://github.com/VILA-Lab/PIXAR-DG
summary: Modern vision-language models (VLMs) have significantly improved image generation and editing capabilities, making pixel-level image tampering detection increasingly important yet challenging under cross-model and out-of-distribution shifts. This work studies domain generalization for pixel-level image tampering detection in modern VLMs like ChatGPT, Gemini, Qwen-Image, etc., aiming to learn tampering localization models that remain robust across diverse VLM-generated manipulation distributions. We propose a simple yet effective domain-generalized training framework built on two practical strategies. First, we introduce a balanced minibatch sampling scheme that strategically samples tampered and real images in each minibatch, preventing biased optimization toward either manipulated artifacts or clean-image priors and avoiding training collapse, ensuring that each optimization step receives proper sampled gradient signals. Second, we adopt a simple late-injection strategy, where the detector is first trained on large-scale base data until stable convergence, and then exposed to a small amount of newly selected supporting data from emerging VLM distributions, improving adaptability without overfitting to limited new domains. Together, these components provide a simple yet strong recipe for improving pixel-level tampering localization and OOD robustness across modern VLMs. Despite the conceptual simplicity, our framework outperforms the prior state-of-the-art PIXAR by a large margin of 26.1% and 26.8% relative improvement in average gIoU and cIoU, respectively, across OOD VLMs of GPT-Images-2.0, Gemini-3.1, FLUX.2, and Seedream 4.5. Our code is available at https://github.com/VILA-Lab/PIXAR-DG

AI.tldr: A domain-generalized training framework for pixel-level tampering detection across diverse VLMs, using balanced minibatch sampling and late-injection strategy, achieving 26.1% and 26.8% relative improvement in gIoU and cIoU over prior SOTA PIXAR across OOD VLMs.
AI.motivation: Pixel-level image tampering detection faces significant challenges under cross-model and out-of-distribution shifts from modern VLMs (ChatGPT, Gemini, Qwen-Image). Existing methods lack robustness across diverse VLM-generated manipulation distributions.
AI.method: (1) Balanced minibatch sampling: strategically samples tampered and real images in each minibatch to prevent biased optimization and training collapse. (2) Late-injection strategy: trains detector on large-scale base data until stable convergence, then exposes to a small amount of supporting data from emerging VLM distributions to improve adaptability without overfitting.
AI.result: Outperforms PIXAR by 26.1% (gIoU) and 26.8% (cIoU) relative improvement across OOD VLMs including GPT-Images-2.0, Gemini-3.1, FLUX.2, and Seedream 4.5.
AI.conclusion: The proposed simple yet effective framework provides a strong recipe for pixel-level tampering localization and OOD robustness across modern VLMs.

title: The Many Senses of Visual Similarity: A Text-Prompted Image Perceptual Metric
summary: Human visual similarity judgments are context-dependent. For example, two images may be similar in shape but distinct in color. Existing perceptual similarity metrics, however, collapse these nuances into a single scalar value, offering no mechanism to condition on specific aspects. To bridge this gap, we introduce a large-scale dataset of human similarity judgments over image triplets, where each triplet is annotated across multiple, free-form semantic aspects of similarity. Benchmarking a broad range of frontier vision-language models (VLMs) reveals a considerable performance gap compared to human annotators' consensus. Leveraging our data, we fine-tune a VLM to produce our Text-Prompted Image Perceptual Similarity (TPIPS) metric, capturing multiple senses of visual similarity depending on the specified text prompt. We demonstrate that TPIPS aligns more closely with human perception and generalizes reliably beyond the training distribution. Finally, we show that TPIPS unlocks new capabilities in text-guided retrieval, compositional search, and the fine-grained evaluation of generative models. Our code, data, and trained models are at https://peterwang512.github.io/TPIPS

AI.tldr: This paper introduces TPIPS, a text-prompted perceptual similarity metric trained on a large-scale dataset of human similarity judgments over image triplets annotated with free-form semantic aspects. It demonstrates that existing VLMs underperform compared to human consensus, and that TPIPS better aligns with human perception and generalizes to new tasks like text-guided retrieval and generative model evaluation.
AI.motivation: Existing perceptual similarity metrics collapse context-dependent aspects (e.g., shape vs. color) into a single scalar, offering no mechanism to condition on specific semantic aspects of similarity.
AI.method: A large-scale dataset of human similarity judgments over image triplets is collected, with each triplet annotated across multiple free-form semantic aspects. A vision-language model (VLM) is fine-tuned on this data to produce the Text-Prompted Image Perceptual Similarity (TPIPS) metric, which takes a text prompt to condition the notion of similarity.
AI.result: Benchmarking frontier VLMs shows a significant gap compared to human consensus. TPIPS aligns more closely with human perception and generalizes reliably beyond the training distribution.
AI.conclusion: TPIPS unlocks new capabilities in text-guided retrieval, compositional search, and fine-grained evaluation of generative models.
